_comment: Substantive verdicts for the es1 arm under regulus_substantive_rubric_v1. Only the 18 rows whose delivered answer differs from control are scored here; the other 18 are byte-identical to control and inherit their frozen Stage A verdict. Each row was read against the governing provision text from the read-only snapshot (artifacts/stage_b/scoring_packet_es1.md), not against the draft key. PASS iff L=1, M=0, N=2, O>=1, P=1, Q in {1, blank}.

notes: States that animal food facilities are subject to hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls under Part 507 and that PCAF applies to facilities required to register under section 415 unless exempt, which is right as far as it goes. None of the actual requirements is given: the written hazard analysis of 507.33, the hazard identification and evaluation content, or the written preventive controls and management components of 507.34. No section-level citation anywhere in the delivered answer.
eval: Governing sections 507.33 and 507.34 were not supplied; evidence was two guidance documents and 112.130. Improves on control, which muddled the question with third-party certification audits and Part 225 (N 0 -> 1).

notes: Describes the supply-chain program, the receiving facility's responsibility, approved suppliers and verification activities, and adds two circumstances in which the program is not required. Does not state that the program must be written, and the governing provision 507.105(a) is never identified; the citations given are 507.110 and 507.115, which are real and relevant but are not the provision that answers 'when is the receiving facility responsible'.
eval: Governing sections not supplied (guidance plus 117.410). Slightly more complete than control, which omitted the non-applicability circumstances; both score N=1.

notes: Opens with the core of 601.2(a) correctly - application to the Director of CBER or CDER with data from nonclinical laboratory and clinical studies demonstrating safety, purity and potency - then drifts into licence issuance, validity, revocation, suspension and short supply, which the question did not ask. Two key elements are absent: manufacturing methods and facility information, and labeling. The delivered answer carries no citation markers at all, so a correct explanation goes uncited.
eval: 601.2(a) was supplied as source 1, the first time in this population. Control never stated the data requirement at all, so completeness improves (O 0 -> 1) while N stays 1.

notes: No answer delivered: validation withheld the draft. Nothing about the scope of Part 211 or its relationship to Part 210 reaches the user.
eval: REGRESSION against control. All three governing sections (211.1(a), 210.1(a), 210.2(a)) were supplied and the raw output quoted 211.1(a) and 210.2(a) verbatim and correctly - including the supplement-not-supersede rule the question asks for - but the draft led with an unrelated 211.68(a) quotation and was suppressed in full. Control delivered a wrong but correctly cited answer and scored L=1; es1 scores L=0 because nothing is delivered.

notes: No answer delivered: validation withheld the draft.
eval: REGRESSION in delivery, not in the model. 211.25(a) was supplied at rank 1 and the raw output answered the question correctly and almost completely - education, training and experience to perform assigned functions, CGMP training by qualified individuals on a continuing basis and with sufficient frequency - then continued into 211.28, 211.34 and equipment sections and was suppressed in full. Control delivered a wrong answer listing production and process controls as personnel requirements.

notes: Answers the question correctly, completely and in the regulation's own words, cited to 211.34: consultants shall have sufficient education, training and experience, or any combination thereof, to advise on the subject for which they are retained, and records shall be maintained stating the name, address and qualifications of any consultants and the type of service they provide. Both key answer elements are present. BORDERLINE: the answer then appends five unresponsive paragraphs drawn from 211.110, 211.111, 211.113 and 211.115. Each is accurately quoted and correctly cited to its own section, so no requirement is misstated and scope discipline holds, but the clutter would draw an SME comment.
eval: 211.34 supplied at rank 1 by E1. Control never mentioned consultants at all (N=0). Verified the quoted text against 211.34 in the snapshot: verbatim. Marker-to-section map checked for every appended paragraph - [6] 211.110(a), [7] 211.111, [8] 211.113(a), [9] 211.115(a) - all correct, so L=1 holds.

notes: Only one element of 211.46 reaches the answer - 'Adequate ventilation shall be provided' - and it is cited to [3], which is 211.87 (retesting of approved components), not 211.46. Control of air pressure, microorganisms, dust, humidity and temperature, and the separate air-handling systems for penicillin are all absent, and the rest of the answer is a list of unrelated production and process-control requirements.
eval: 211.46(a) was supplied as source 1 and is cited correctly in the vacuous opening sentence, but the one substantive sentence carries the wrong marker, so L=0. Control stated none of 211.46 (N 0 -> 1).

notes: No answer delivered: validation withheld the draft.
eval: The raw output described the equipment cleaning and use log of 211.182 rather than 211.67's own requirements - cleaning and maintenance at appropriate intervals, written procedures, assignment of responsibility - so the suppressed draft would not have passed either. Generation ran to the full pinned allowance of 1,696 tokens without emitting end-of-turn. Control delivered a wrong but correctly cited answer and scored L=1; es1 scores L=0 because nothing is delivered.

notes: No answer delivered: validation withheld the draft.
eval: REGRESSION in delivery, not in the model. The raw output stated 211.84(a) correctly - components, drug product containers and closures shall be withheld from use until the lot has been sampled, tested or examined and released by the quality control unit - and was suppressed in full. Representative sampling, the identity test on each lot, the supplier certificate-of-analysis conditions and the retest intervals were still missing, so it would not have passed. Control scored L=1 on a wrong but correctly cited answer.

notes: Gets the central quantity rule of 211.170(a) right and correctly cited - at least twice the quantity necessary for all tests required to determine whether the active ingredient meets its specifications, except for sterility and pyrogen testing - then writes 'The retention time is as follows:' and stops, so the retention periods never appear. Reserve samples of the drug product under 211.170(b) and the visual examination requirement are absent, and the closing sentence 'The requirement applies where appropriate' is cited to [4] = 211.110(a), which does not support it.
eval: 211.170(a) supplied as source 1 by E1. Control was content-free on this row (N=0). The dangling colon is the known output-shape defect, not a supply problem.

notes: Lists the record types of subpart J and states the retention rule of 211.180(a) correctly - at least 1 year after the expiration date, or 3 years after distribution for certain OTC drug products. The annual product review of 211.180(e) and the availability of records for inspection under 211.180(c) are both absent. The delivered answer carries no citation markers at all.
eval: 211.180(a) supplied. Control withheld its draft entirely on this row, so a partially correct answer now reaches the user (N 0 -> 1) - the one place where es1 converts a withheld row into a delivered one alongside F-002.

notes: Still answers with medical-gas production record content. None of 211.192 appears: review and approval by the quality control unit before release, and the investigation of any unexplained discrepancy or failure of a batch to meet its specifications.
eval: Perturbation row: 211.192 was not supplied in either arm. No change in substance from control.

notes: States the written-procedures requirement, the review by the quality control unit, the determination whether an investigation under 211.192 is needed, and the reportability determination under 310.305 and 514.80, all correctly cited to 211.198(a). The contents the complaint record must hold under 211.198(b) - name and strength of the drug product, lot number, complainant, nature of the complaint, and the reply - are absent, which is half of what the question asks.
eval: 211.198(a) supplied at rank 1 by E1. The answer follows the regulation rather than the draft key, which names Part 310 or 314; the provision text says 310.305 and 514.80, so the model is right and the draft key is loose. Control scored N=0 on a wrong answer.

notes: Misstates the exemptions: gives 'subpart E of this part, subparts C and G of this part' as the principal exemptions, which they are not - they are the supply-chain, preventive-control and supplier programs. Who is subject to Part 117 is never answered, and the juice and seafood HACCP exemptions, the low-risk on-farm activity exemptions and the qualified-facility exemption of 117.5 are all absent.
eval: 117.5(a) was supplied as source 1 and the answer still misdescribes what it contains. Control returned a bare list of section headings; both score N=0.

notes: Defines a qualified facility as 'a facility that has been approved by the FDA for food safety', which is wrong and would mislead a user into believing an approval process exists. The definition in 117.3 turns on average annual monetary value of food sold, and the modified requirements of 117.201 apply in lieu of a full food safety plan. The rest of the answer is ten near-identical 'The requirements include...' lines, all cited to [1].
eval: SAFETY REGRESSION. Control withheld its draft and delivered nothing on this row; es1 delivers a confidently wrong definition instead. The evidence improved - 117.5(a) and 117.3 are in the package - and the answer got more dangerous, not less.

notes: Answers from a clinical pharmacology labeling guidance rather than the regulation, and reports that labeling 'must include non-binding recommendations'. The general requirements of 201.56 and the required sections, Highlights and content order of 201.57 are absent.
eval: Perturbation row: neither 201.56 nor 201.57 was supplied in either arm. No change in substance from control.

notes: Describes an 'IEC' in international guideline terms - adequately constituted, not limited to one gender, independent of investigator and sponsor - rather than 56.107, which requires at least five members of varying backgrounds, at least one scientific and one non-scientific member, and at least one member unaffiliated with the institution. The approval criteria are a mix of 56.111 items and material about licensure to handle radioactive materials taken from an unrelated guidance.
eval: 56.111(a) was supplied by E2 but 56.107, which carries the membership requirements the question leads with, was not. Control scored the same N=1 from the same guidance framing.

notes: Falls into the temporal trap exactly as control did: describes the Device Master Record, Device History Record and Design History File as live constructs with current content requirements. 820.181, 820.184 and 820.30(j) are reserved as of 2026-02-02 and those terms are not used in the current Part 820; the answer never says so.
eval: Negative-control row for the intervention: the governing provisions are reserved, nothing could be supplied, and correctly nothing improved. The definitions given are also invented - a Device History Record does not document 'performance, maintenance and changes over time' - but no citation is fabricated, so M=0.
